newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Iran says U.S. seeks to justify permanence in Gulf.
newsitem.headline: Iran says U.S. seeks to justify permanence in Gulf.

text.p: Iran said on Wednesday the United States was pursuing far-reaching objectives in Iraq which included a justification for maintaining a permanent presence in the Gulf.

State-run Tehran radio, monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation, said in a commentary after Wednesday's second U.S. missile raid on southern Iraq: "By continuing its attacks against Iraq, America is pursuing objectives far beyond stopping the Iraqi military operations in the city of Arbil.

"With this action, (President Bill) Clinton not only takes personal advantage of developments in Iraq, he also paves the way for the advancement of the long-term U.S. strategy for maintaining a permanent presence in the Persian Gulf region."
The United States has dozens of warships in and around the Gulf with 20,000 armed forces personnel on board and stationed at land bases, mainly in Saudi Arabia.
The two American attacks on Iraq were launched from U.S. Navy ships and air force B-52 bombers.

Tehran radio said Iraqi President Saddam Hussein had committed another mistake: he had once again become involved in the killing of the innocent people of his country, and that had provided America with the excuse to strengthen its presence in the Gulf.

"America is taking Saddam Hussein's actions as a justification, and under the pretext of instability in the region, is justifying its presence in the Persian Gulf. It uses the regional countries' resources to achieve its long-term objectives in the Middle East," the radio said.
It accused Clinton of taking advantage of the situation to prove he was a strong leader for electoral purposes.
"During the last four years Clinton has been criticised repeatedly by opponents for his failures and weaknesses in foreign policy," the radio said.
Military action against Iraq "shows Clinton's determination to push U.S. foreign policy forward for campaigning purposes".
